days.label: Brit
days.key: And I will establish My covenant between Me and thee and thy seed after thee throughout their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God unto thee and to thy seed after thee.
days.s: In Genesis 17 God appears to Abram, renames him Abraham and promises him nations and land; Sforno, on Genesis 17:7, reads His promise to be their God as binding His name to them without intermediary, so that, keeping the covenant, they endure for ever.
days.src: Sforno, Commentary on the Torah, Genesis 17:7, Hebrew (On Your Way), Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Shabbat
days.key: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.
days.s: Among the ten words spoken at Sinai, this one opens the command about the seventh day; Rashi, on Exodus 20:8, takes ‘Remember’ as a charge to keep the day always in mind, setting aside for it any fine thing that comes to hand.
days.src: Rashi, Commentary on the Torah, Exodus 20:8, Hebrew (Rosenbaum and Silbermann, 1929 to 1934), Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

days.label: Rosh Hashanah
days.key: Speak unto the children of Israel, saying: In the seventh month, in the first day of the month, shall be a solemn rest unto you, a memorial proclaimed with the blast of horns, a holy convocation.
days.s: Among the seasons appointed through Moses, this one follows Passover and the seven weeks; Rashi, on Leviticus 23:24, reads the memorial as verses of remembrance and of the horn, with the binding of Isaac recalled for Israel’s sake, and Ramban, there, as the blast itself, a remembrance before God on the day He judges, with pardon in the ten days.
days.src: Rashi (Rosenbaum and Silbermann, 1929 to 1934) and Ramban (On Your Way New), on the Torah, Leviticus 23:24, Hebrew, Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)
